title: The naive framing: "Claude learned to judge compliance risk"
text: You guess Claude learned to judge compliance risk from a skill called gaps. It didn't. It was handed a file of instructions. Gaps just names one such file. Let's see what's actually inside it. Here Claude has a gaps skill and it

title: Sounds like judgment
text: Sounds like it can now weigh regulations and decide what counts as a compliance gap on its own.

title: Broken, with a case — delete the folder, nothing is lost
text: But nothing in the model changes. Delete the skills folder and Claude loses no compliance judgment. There was none to lose. It just stops following that one tracking routine.

title: The anchor: one file — gaps's single SKILL.md
text: Here's what a skill actually is, one file. Gaps for instance is a folder holding a single skill. MD instructions for opening a tracker, reporting what's flagged and not yet closed, and updating an item when you close it or risk accept

title: Read it, then follow it in order
text: It. Claude reads that file top to bottom and works through it step by step in the order it's written, no branching unless the file itself says branch. That makes

title: Spec, not power — the payoff and the limit
text: A skill a specification, not a new power. The payoff, the same tracker check every time what's open, what's closed, what's been risk accepted. The limit, anything outside those written steps and Claude is off the map. So gaps

title: The anchor returns — same file, every run
text: Never taught Claude how to judge a compliance risk. It just guarantees that every time gaps runs, Claude reads that same file and reports the tracker the same way. That's the whole trick.

title: Both directions — neither one is proof
text: Watching Claude close out a gap cleanly doesn't prove it understood the underlying risk. A file can be followed to the letter on a case it never really evaluated. And watching it mishandle a tracker update doesn't prove the skill is broken. It may just be a case the file steps don't cover.

title: Carry-out
text: A skill doesn't teach Claude how to judge compliance risk. It's a file of steps Claude reads before it starts. So every tracker check comes out the same way every time. Your turn. Paste this

title: Your turn
text: Into Claude. Pick one status check I run the same way every time. Write me a skill MD for it, plain language ordered steps, then read it back to me and walk me through exactly what you'll do before you do it. Claude gaps Liam in for bear.
